finding.claim: A verifier built with key '' or null and a configured algorithms list accepts unsigned tokens. The falsy key skips the empty-key guard and makes hasKey false, and an empty signature skips verifySignature, so a token like base64url({"alg":"HS256"}).base64url({"sub":"admin"}). is accepted. Conditional on misconfiguration; async key functions are protected.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled token with an empty third (signature) segment; precondition: static key is '' or null and algorithms is non-empty
finding.sink: verifyToken acceptance of the payload as authenticated (verifier.js:426 return of payload)

trace.note: if (key && keyType !== 'function') is false for '' or null, so prepareKeyOrSecret and its empty-secret guard are skipped
BASE64URL_RE is * and matches an empty signature segment, so decode succeeds
hasKey = !!key is false
!hasKey && signature is false because signature is '', so no missingKey error
alg 'HS256' is in allowedAlgorithms, so the algorithm check passes
if (signature && ...) is false, so verifySignature never runs
claim validators pass and the payload is returned as valid

finding.guards_checked: Algorithm allowlist (passes, attacker only needs an allowed name). Empty-key guard at verifier.js:38-40 (bypassed by falsy short-circuit). hasKey && !signature check at verifier.js:274 (inactive when key is falsy). Decoder base64url check (accepts empty). Async path is protected: a key function returning '' goes through prepareKeyOrSecret and is rejected. Not verified by execution (no shell available).

finding.claim: With caching enabled, a token cached without an iat is served from cache after its exp has passed, for up to cacheTTL (default 600000 ms). The cache TTL ignores exp when iat is absent and the cache-hit path does not re-run exp validation. Conditional on cache being enabled (off by default) and iat-less tokens (noTimestamp or external issuer).
finding.source: Attacker holds a once-valid iat-less token with exp; precondition: cache option enabled
finding.sink: Cache hit at verifier.js:364-378 returns the cached payload as valid without re-validating exp

trace.note: hasIat = payload && typeof payload.iat === 'number' is false
The block that reads exp into cacheValue[2] is skipped; cacheValue[2] stays 0
maxTTL = clockTimestamp + clockTolerance + cacheTTL; cacheValue[2] = maxTTL since it is 0
Cache lookup happens before decode and verifyToken
Hit condition: min === 0 and now <= max, true until creation time + cacheTTL, so exp is not checked

finding.guards_checked: Cache is off by default (createCache at verifier.js:83-86 returns null for undefined). exp is honored when iat is present (verifier.js:124-127). Cache key is the full token (hashToken), so the attacker cannot alter the token without changing the key. Validator path is skipped on hit.

finding.claim: Claim validators for aud, iss, sub, jti, nonce, and maxAge (iat) are skipped when the claim is absent from the payload, so tokens lacking the claim pass the allowedAud/allowedIss/etc. checks unless requiredClaims also lists the claim. Design footgun; severity depends on whether tokens without these claims exist under the same key.
finding.source: Validly signed token from the same key that lacks the aud/iss/sub/jti/nonce/iat claim; precondition: verifier sets allowedX or maxAge without requiredClaims
finding.sink: Authorization/scoping decision (audience, issuer, subject, maxAge check)

trace.note: Loop over validators
if (!(claim in payload)) continue skips the validator entirely
maxAge validator on iat is only pushed when maxAge is a number
allowedJti/aud/iss/sub/nonce validators only pushed when option set; no presence enforcement
requiredClaims presence check is opt-in; the library does not force presence by default

finding.guards_checked: Signature and algorithm checks pass (token is genuinely signed by the key). requiredClaims is the only mechanism to force presence and is off by default. Comment at verifier.js:309-310 assumes presence was checked earlier, which holds only when requiredClaims is set.

finding.claim: Signature segments are only checked against the base64url alphabet, not for canonical encoding of trailing pad bits, so each valid signature has alternate valid encodings (3 for HS256). The verifier accepts all of them, making tokens malleable. Impact is limited to applications that key replay or revocation on the raw token string.
finding.source: Attacker holds any valid token and changes the last signature character to an equivalent pad-bit variant
finding.sink: Application logic keyed on raw token string (replay/revocation/single-use); signature acceptance at verifier.js:169

trace.note: BASE64URL_RE permits any alphabet character, including the non-canonical final character
Signature segment passes the alphabet check
Buffer.from(signature, 'base64') decodes leniently, ignoring trailing pad bits
timingSafeEqual on decoded bytes returns true for the variant
Comment claims the signature is canonical after the decoder check, which is not true for pad bits

finding.guards_checked: Alphabet check rejects '=' padding and non-alphabet characters. Constant-time comparison is used. Canonical trailing-bit check is absent.

finding.claim: The signer accepts an empty Buffer as an HMAC secret, while the verifier rejects empty secrets (verifier.js:38-40). Tokens minted with an empty key are forgeable by anyone. Plausible; not confirmed by execution, and it depends on Node's createSecretKey accepting a zero-length buffer.
finding.source: Application passes Buffer.alloc(0) (or an empty secret buffer) as the signing key
finding.sink: Token minting with a publicly known HMAC key

trace.note: !key is false for an empty Buffer; keyType check does not reject Buffer
Buffer case passes validation
detectPrivateKeyAlgorithm returns HS256 for empty content (crypto.js:89)
prepareKeyOrSecret calls createSecretKey on the empty buffer (crypto.js:47)

finding.guards_checked: Empty-secret guard exists only on the verifier side (verifier.js:38-40). Signer has no length check. Empty string '' is rejected at signer.js:216 by !key.

finding.claim: With caching enabled, passing a Buffer token throws a TypeError from hashToken, because Buffer has no split method. This happens before decoding and outside any try/catch, so it bypasses TokenError handling even in callback mode. Availability bug, low severity.
finding.source: Application passes a Buffer token (e.g. raw request body) to verify with cache enabled

trace.note: Buffer tokens are accepted by the type check
cache.get(cacheKeyBuilder(token)) is called inside if (cache) before decode
token.split('.', 1) on a Buffer throws TypeError

finding.guards_checked: Non-string/non-Buffer tokens are rejected at verifier.js:353. The Buffer case is not handled in the cache path. Only applies when cache is enabled.
